cards.ja: メキシコの菓子パン（パン・ドゥルセ）

cards.en: I'm here traveling for two weeks.
cards.ja: 私は2週間の旅行でここに来ています。
cards.glossEn: I'm here traveling for two weeks.

cards.en: How long have you lived in this neighborhood?
cards.ja: この近所にはどのくらい住んでいらっしゃいますか？
cards.glossEn: How long have you lived in this neighborhood?

cards.en: And what do you do for a living?
cards.ja: それで、お仕事は何をされていますか？
cards.glossEn: And what do you do for a living?

cards.ja: 本当ですか？もっと聞かせてください。

cards.en: What do you recommend I visit around here?
cards.ja: この辺りで、どこを訪ねるのがおすすめですか？
cards.glossEn: What do you recommend I visit around here?

cards.en: It was a pleasure chatting with you.
cards.ja: お話しできて楽しかったです。
cards.glossEn: It was a pleasure chatting with you.

reader.en: Every morning, Don Ramón, a retiree and neighbor from the neighborhood, has his coffee at the same table.
reader.ja: 毎朝、退職者で近所の人でもあるドン・ラモンは、いつも同じテーブルでコーヒーを飲みます。
reader.glossEn: Every morning, Don Ramón, a retiree and neighbor from the neighborhood, has his coffee at the same table.

reader.en: Today he asks me where I'm from, and I tell him: I'm from Canada and I'm here traveling for two weeks.
reader.ja: 今日、彼は私にどこの出身かと尋ね、私は彼に言います。「カナダ出身です。2週間の旅行でここに来ています。」
reader.glossEn: Today he asks me where I'm from, and I tell him: I'm from Canada and I'm here traveling for two weeks.

reader.en: Then I ask him: How long have you lived in this neighborhood?
reader.ja: それから私は彼に尋ねます。「この近所にはどのくらい住んでいらっしゃいますか？」
reader.glossEn: Then I ask him: How long have you lived in this neighborhood?

reader.en: He tells me that he has lived here for 40 years and that he was a teacher at the school on the plaza.
reader.ja: 彼は私に、ここに40年住んでいること、そして広場の学校で教師をしていたことを話してくれます。
reader.glossEn: He tells me that he has lived here for 40 years and that he was a teacher at the school on the plaza.

reader.en: Since his work interests me, I say: Really? Tell me more.
reader.ja: 彼の仕事に興味があるので、私は言います。「本当ですか？もっと聞かせてください。」
reader.glossEn: Since his work interests me, I say: Really? Tell me more.

reader.en: Then he talks to me about the market, because on Saturdays they sell very good pan dulce.
reader.ja: それから彼は市場のことを話してくれます。土曜日には、とてもおいしいパン・ドゥルセが売られているからです。
reader.glossEn: Then he talks to me about the market, because on Saturdays they sell very good pan dulce.

reader.en: When I ask him what he recommends, he says that if I have time, I should visit the downtown museum.
reader.ja: 何がおすすめかと尋ねると、彼は、時間があれば中心部の博物館に行くといいと言います。
reader.glossEn: When I ask him what he recommends, he says that if I have time, I should visit the downtown museum.

reader.en: Before I leave, I pay the bill and tell him: It was a pleasure chatting with you.
reader.ja: 帰る前に、私は会計を済ませ、彼に言います。「お話しできて楽しかったです。」
reader.glossEn: Before I leave, I pay the bill and tell him: It was a pleasure chatting with you.

issues: Current source is a first-person narrative with Don Ramón, Canada, two weeks, forty years and the plaza school. Archived generic two-person dialogue changes the scene and is reference-only.

Source card cafecito is affectionate Mexican coffee wording; neutral Japanese コーヒー loses its diminutive. Qualified locale/dictionary reviewer should choose whether to preserve it in a note, without treating Spanish morphology as Japanese grammar.
Pan dulce is Mexican bakery sweet bread; メキシコの菓子パン（パン・ドゥルセ） identifies the food but food/locale review remains open.
The source card And what do you do for a living? is in the card list but not in the eight-turn Reader. Preserve the card without inventing a Reader conversation turn.
Town square/plaza is 広場; whether 町の広場 is preferred needs qualified review. Downtown museum is 中心部の博物館, not a new named venue.
The source Reader says Don Ramón was a teacher, but the card work is generic. The Japanese Reader keeps the past-tense teacher fact.

Retiree, neighbor, older-person register, direct Japanese speech, and polite closing require qualified Japanese review. The source does not require asking private details beyond the authored questions.
This is unapproved source-only draft; six authored modes, forms, speaking, contextual dictionary, saved-item policy, exact-text audio and distinct listening remain open.

Opus flagged 市場 reading ambiguity; the physical-market reading いちば must be pinned for eventual furigana and TTS, but this inert packet has no reading field. Fable agreed the issue belongs in review rather than silently changing the face.
Fable corrected Reader 7 from a yes/no recommendation question to the source what-question. Other Opus style proposals were held pending qualified Japanese review, and no source facts were added.
